title: Professional Email Pro Upgrade to the Top Product of a Family
content:
**Scope.** A Pro upgrade is the move of a Professional Email subscription up to the top product of its family, Harborline Mail Pro from Harborline Mail Starter or Plus and Microsoft 365 Business Premium from Microsoft 365 Business Basic or Standard, and this rule prices only a Pro upgrade; every other move up remains under the product change rules.

**Rule.** A Pro upgrade may be made only while the subscription status is active, and once it is billed the subscription's product is the target product, Harborline Mail Pro for a Harborline Mail subscription and Microsoft 365 Business Premium for a Microsoft 365 one, for the rest of the term on the same billing plan and term dates, every seat on the subscription being upgraded. The Pro upgrade charge is fixed only after the subscription stands active on a paid term whose term end date lies after today. Once the agent has quoted the Pro upgrade charge, the account holder pays it personally at Harborline's secure checkout with PayPal, a payment method Harborline never stores on the account, and the upgrade takes effect when that payment completes.

Put another way: while the subscription record does not show it active on a paid term ending later than today, no Pro upgrade charge is fixed.

## Tool: `upgrade_mail_product_74224a57`

**Capability.** The account holder pays, personally at Harborline's secure checkout with PayPal, the move of their email subscription up to the top product of its family: Harborline Mail Pro for a Harborline Mail Starter or Plus subscription, Microsoft 365 Business Premium for a Microsoft 365 Business Basic or Standard one. One call books one upgrade billing line covering and billing every licensed seat from today to the term end date, paid by PayPal, and switches the subscription's product to the target product at once; the seat count, billing plan and term dates do not change.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it at checkout.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `email_plan_id` | reference number of the customer's email subscription being moved up, as returned by the email subscription lookup and read out to the customer by the agent | identifier |
| `upgrade_amount` | the upgrade amount to bill, in US dollars | positive number with 2 decimal places; more decimals are rounded half up to the cent before booking |

**Return.** On success: "Upgraded subscription <email_plan_id> to <product>: upgrade line <email_charge_id> order <order_ref> for <amount> USD covering <seats> seats to <term_end>, paid by PayPal." The product is the target product's official name, the order reference HL- followed by 8 digits and the term end YYYY-MM-DD. A reply starting with "Error:" means nothing was booked: an unknown subscription, a subscription already on the top product of its family, or a non-positive amount.

## Points of judgement

- A Harborline Mail Pro or Microsoft 365 Business Premium subscription has no Pro upgrade.
- Every seat on the subscription moves up; a Pro upgrade of part of the seats does not exist.
